messages.subject: lavTestLRT multilevel?
parts:
Hi there

I tried to compare two two-level models, nested an level 2

# Leermodell, nur Kovariate #
model <- '
            level: 1
            PoFGsum~PrFGsum
           
            level: 2
            PoFGsum~PrFGsum'

# MLR, multipel imputiert (robust) #
fit.leer <-sem.mi(model, Imp.Struktur, cluster="ID_C", estimator="MLR")#
summary(fit.leer, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, rsquareAdj=TRUE)#

# Ein Prädiktor (Total)
model <- '
            level: 1
            PoFGsum~PrFGsum
           
            level: 2
            PoFGsum~PrFGsum+Total'

# MLR, multipel imputiert (robust) #
fit.eins <-sem.mi(model, Imp.Struktur, cluster="ID_C", estimator="MLR")#
summary(fit.eins, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, rsquareAdj=TRUE)#



LRT_result <- lavTestLRT.mi(fit.eins, h1=fit.leer,asymptotic=FALSE,test="D2", pool.robust = TRUE)
print(LRT_result) 

This caused the following error message: models have equal degrees of freedom

In my eyes this is not the case - the dfs are different. I tried also to compare several other two level models, variing predictors on both levels. Because I always got the same error message I guess that it is caused by the incompatibility of the function with two level models. A quick look at the source code support my guess. Am I right? Are there alternative methods to test wether the R^2 values of the two models differ significantly - especially on level 2?

Thanks

Maurus

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavTestLRT multilevel?
parts:
The models are fitted to different data, which should lead to an error even if the df were to differ.  The model with the additional Level-2 predictor "Total" is attempting to reproduce a 3 x 3 Level-2 covariance matrix, whereas the model without "Total" is attempting to reproduce a 2 x 2 Level-2 covariance matrix.  When you add "Total", there are 3 more elements in the 3 x 3 Level-2 covariance matrix (variance of Total, and its 2 covariances with the other 2 variables).  However, the models have the same df because the larger model estimates 3 additional parameters (the slope of Total on the DV, the variance of Total, and its covariance with the other predictor).
